title: Strictly No Elephants
teacherNotes: Communicate with classmates about a story (SEL7), demonstrate eagerness and curiosity (APL2), and act out characters and events (RL.PK.3). Seat children around the perimeter of the rug. Select several scenes from the beginning, middle, and end to act out; the source leaves the scene choices to the teacher. Consider what was successful or challenging, how each child participated (including as an audience member), and what new understandings children gained through acting and their reflection afterward.

steps.title: Before Reading · Act Out the Story
steps.prompt: We will read Strictly No Elephants again. And this time, we will act the story out.
steps.note: We will act out many stories this year! When we act out stories, we pretend to be characters in the story.

steps.title: Our Audience and Stage
steps.prompt: Around the edge is our audience. Inside is our stage.
steps.note: We are sitting at the perimeter, or around the edge, as the audience, the people who will watch the story. Inside of the perimeter will be the stage, where we will act the story out.

steps.title: You Can Say “Pass”
steps.prompt: If you don’t want to act, you can say “pass” or use a gesture.
steps.note: As I read, I will invite children from around the circle to enter the stage and play a character from the book. Show a gesture children can use to pass their turn, such as shaking their head, putting up a hand, or crossing hands to shoulders.

steps.title: Let’s Get Started
steps.note: Teacher: Select several scenes (beginning, middle, end) to act out. Use the original pages to support the scenes you choose. The lesson does not prescribe specific scenes or page-bound teaching stops.

steps.title: Cover
steps.note: Teacher: Select several scenes from the beginning, middle, and end to act out. Invite children to play characters; children may pass or participate as audience members.
